new_statements.quote: § 2. Die Accente sind dynamische Wortaccente. Nur die betonten Silben sind hier mit Acut bezeichnet. Es gibt jedoch einige Wörter, die sich nur durch die Töne unterscheiden.
new_statements.translation: § 2. The accents are dynamic word accents. Only the stressed syllables are marked here with an acute. There are, however, some words that are distinguished only by their tones.
new_statements.citation: Müller, P. Fr. [Franz], S.V.D. 1906. Ein Beitrag zur Kenntnis der Akasele (Tšambá)-Sprache. Mit Zusätzen von P. W. Schmidt. Anthropos 1: 787-803.
new_statements.locator: p. 789, II. Skizze der Grammatik, A. Lautverhältnisse, § 2
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (archive.org scan of Anthropos 1, 1906, printed page 789). The page reads, at the head of the page under the running head "— 789 —": "§ 2. Die Accente sind dynamische Wortaccente. Nur die | [be]tonten Silben sind hier mit Acut bezeichnet. Es gibt jedoch | [eini]ge Wörter, die sich nur durch die Töne unterscheiden." The scan's left margin clips the first two or three letters of lines 2-3 ("betonten", "einige"); both independent scanned files supply them in full ( ll. 109-111; ll. 45668-45670, second archive.org scan), so the quote is verbatim as reported. Locator is right: p. 789, section II. Skizze der Grammatik, A. Lautverhältnisse (heading on p. 788, scanned ll. 60-63), § 2, follow…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Müller claims that Akasele word accent is dynamic (stress) rather than musical, marks 'stressed' syllables with an acute, and adds that a few words are distinguished by tone alone. He gives no rule for where the accent falls. His own wordlist puts acutes on several syllables of one word (óbóyá 'king', ómómóàlé 'liar', bíníkpólé 'murderers'), so the marks in practice look like high-tone marks; the modern SIL description (Songhai Apou 2018) treats the language as a two-tone language and says nothing about stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None beyond the note that some words differ only by tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (Wortaccente), citation forms in a wordlist and short grammatical sketch; a 1906 missionary sketch edited by P. W. Schmidt, based on Tchamba town speech, with Tem as the elicitation language.
new_statements.identity_note: Müller 1906 describes the speech of Tchamba (Tšambá) town, the central Akaselem canton, called Akaselecé by its speakers; Müller notes it is said to be the same language as that of Bassari (Ntcham, ntch1242) with only small dialect differences. Songhai Apou 2018 covers the same variety (Tchamba and Laarɩnɩ cantons). Glottolog akas1242 = ISO aks; PHOIBLE names it 'Akasilimi' after Podi's title.

new_statements.quote: [p. 66, par. 17] Wörter, die sich nur durch verschiedenen Ton unterscheiden, sind infolge der durch die Affixe eingetretenen Differenzierung der Wörter auch hier seltener; trotzdem treten jedoch wie im Tobote die Töne, besonders auch die der Nasale, deutlich hervor. [...] [p. 66, footnote 1] Mü. sagt über Ton und Akzent: „Die Accente sind dynamische Wortaccente. Nur die betonten Silben sind hier mit Accent bezeichnet. Es gibt jedoch einige Wörter, die sich nur durch die Töne unterscheiden“. Mü. hat in einer ganzen Reihe von Wörtern jede Silbe des Wortes mit einem Akut versehen. — In den von Mü. übernommenen Wörtern habe ich die Akzent- oder Tonzeichen weggelassen.
new_statements.translation: [par. 17] Words that are distinguished only by different tone are rarer here too, because of the differentiation of words brought about by the affixes; nevertheless, as in Tobote, the tones, especially those of the nasals, stand out clearly. [...] [fn. 1] Mü[ller] says about tone and accent: 'The accents are dynamic word accents. Only the stressed syllables are marked here with an accent. There are, however, some words that are distinguished only by the tones.' Mü[ller] has, in a whole series of words, put an acute on every syllable of the word. — In the words taken over from Mü[ller] I have left out the accent or tone marks.
new_statements.citation: Westermann, Diedrich. 1922. Die Akasele-Sprache in Nordtogo. In: Die Sprache der Guang in Togo und auf der Goldküste und fünf andere Togosprachen, pp. 60-97. Berlin: Reimer.
new_statements.locator: p. 66, 'Der Ton', par. 17-18 and footnote 1; par. 20 continues on p. 67 (second pagination run of the volume; running head 'Akasele.' / 'Grammatik.')
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the saved Google Books page scan (printed p. 66, running head 'Akasele.') and inspected it directly, plus the per-page scanned. Both quoted passages are on p. 66 exactly as reported: par. 17 'Woerter, die sich nur durch verschiedenen Ton unterscheiden, sind infolge der durch die Affixe eingetretenen Differenzierung der Woerter auch hier seltener; trotzdem treten jedoch wie im Tobote die Toene, besonders auch die der Nasale, deutlich hervor.' and footnote 1 under the heading 'Der Ton 1)': 'Mue. sagt ueber Ton und Akzent: "Die Accente sind dynamische Wortaccente. Nur die betonten Silben sind hier mit Accent bezeichnet. Es gibt jedoch einige Woerter, die sich nur durch die Toene untersc…
new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog (Akasele, empty rule; existing statement = Müller 1906 'tone language with a stress statement'): Westermann confirms the language is tonal with tone-only minimal pairs and adds detail (H/L plus a final mid tone, tonal number marking, H-L-H word melody). On stress he adds nothing positive: he only relays Müller's 'dynamische Wortaccente' sentence in a footnote, remarks that Müller's acutes sit on every syllable of many words, and omits those marks; no stress position is given, so the catalog's empty placement rule stands. He does not explicitly deny word stress, so this is not scored as a contradiction, but his own description is tone-only.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Westermann analyses Akasele (Kaselem) as a tone language: high and low (and a mid tone on the final syllable of some disyllables), lexical minimal pairs by tone alone (p. 66 par. 18: bó 'be ill' / bò 'surface, on'; kó 'cough' / kò 'be dry'; ákó 'hoes' / àkò 'parrot'), singular vs plural distinguished only by the tone of the nasal affix (par. 17, 19), and a high-low-high word melody as in Tobote (par. 20-21, pp. 66-67). He states no word-stress rule and no stress position of his own; the only mention of accent is footnote 1 on p. 66, which quotes Müller 1906's 'dynamic word accents' claim and adds that Müller put an acute on every syllable of many words, and that Westermann dropped Müller's accent/tone marks. The phonology section 'Die Laute' (par. 1-16, pp. 60-66) contains nothing on Akzent/Betonung (scanned keyword search over pp. 59-73: the footnote is the only hit).
new_statements.exceptions: none for stress; for tone: some nouns change tone in the plural (par. 19), the low-toned plural suffix -m becomes high to fit the high-low-high melody (par. 21), certain disyllables take a mid tone on the last syllable instead of low-high (par. 20-21).
new_statements.identity_note: Westermann's data come from a single speaker from the town of Tschamba (recorded in Lome, first half of 1907); speakers call the area 'Kaselem' and the language atje 'speech' (p. 60). Same variety as the catalog's Akasele/Akaselem (akas1242); Westermann compares it throughout with Tobote (Bassari, i.e. Ntcham), a separate language.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement on placement, because no source gives one. The only tension is of type: Müller 1906 (Anthropos 1, p. 789) calls the accents 'dynamische Wortaccente' while conceding that some words differ only by tone; Westermann 1922 (p. 66-67) describes Akasele purely as a tone language (high/low/mid, tonal minimal pairs, tonal number marking, H-L-H melody), quotes Müller's accent sentence only in a footnote, notes that Müller marked every syllable of many words with an acute, and drops those marks, i.e. he does not adopt the dynamic-accent analysis. The SIL orthography guides (2018, 2019, read in the earlier reading) likewise describe two tones and say nothing about stress. So: tonal by every source; one early stress assertion (Müller) with no position and not endorsed by the later description.

sources.note: p. 789 §2: accents are dynamic word accents; only the stressed syllables are marked with an acute; a few words differ only by tone. No rule for where the accent falls. The wordlist that follows carries acutes on several syllables per word (óbóyá 'König', ómómóàlé 'Lügner', bíníkpólé 'Mörder', bíkpálé 'Farmer' pl.), so in practice the marks behave like high-tone marks rather than a single word stress.

sources.citation: Songhai A., Laré Aminou. 2019. Guide de transition Français-Akaselem, 3e édition (livret). SIL Togo-Bénin. 32 pp. Leçon 1b 'Les tons en akaselem', p. 8.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; two tones (haut/bas) marked on all vowels and syllabic nasals; four tone combinations on long vowels; lexical and grammatical tone pairs.

sources.citation: Songhai Apou, Laré (Aminou). 2018. Guide d'orthographe de l'akaselem (tchamba). Kara: SIL Togo-Bénin. 39 pp. §3 'Tons', pp. 14-15.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'L'akaselem.. est une langue à tons.. On distingue en akaselem deux tons pertinents, à savoir : haut et bas.' Lexical minimal pairs (ɩ́wɛ́ɛ́ 'paroles' / ɩ́wɛɛ 'maladie', káá 'annoncer' / kaa 'compter') and grammatical tone (subjunctive, perfective, reflexive). 'accent' appears only as 'accent aigu' (the diacritic). Tone marking called provisional. Data from Tchamba and Laarɩnɩ cantons.
